newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Duhalde consults Cavallo on "mafias".
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Duhalde consults Cavallo on "mafias".

text.p: Eduardo Duhalde, governor of Buenos Aires Province and presidential candidate for 1999, said in an interview published Friday he had consulted former economy minister Domingo Cavallo on corruption in Argentina.

Cavallo, sacked last July, has implicated former cabinet colleagues, federal judges and ruling Peronist Party officials close to Duhalde in his campaign against "mafias," or crime rings, inside the Argentine administration.
"I simply wanted to hear Cavallo himself explain some of the statements he makes," Duhalde, second-in-command of the Peronist Party and former vice-president, told Clarin daily.
"In a democracy like ours, I believe there are things that have to be cleared up, whether it's true or not," he said.

Cavallo has also accused President Carlos Menem of being aware of some of the wrongdoing and not fighting corruption hard enough. But Duhalde, involved in a silent battle with Menem to stop attempts to get Menem re-elected again, said he was not trying to take sides by meeting with Cavallo.
Acknowledging that Cavallo's relationship with Menem's government was "not at its best moment," Duhalde added:
"But I don't want to get involved in infighting between Cavallo and some members of the government."
